title: Covering Indexes & Index-Only Scans
description: Achieve Index-Only Scans using the INCLUDE clause to eliminate table heap lookups entirely.

data.text: When an index satisfies a `WHERE` condition, PostgreSQL still has to perform a **Heap Fetch** (read the physical table page) to retrieve any projected columns not present in the index. An **Index-Only Scan** occurs when ALL requested columns are present in the index, allowing the query engine to skip table heap reads completely.

Before PostgreSQL 11, adding payload columns to an index meant including them in the B-tree search key, increasing tree depth and slowing down writes. The **`INCLUDE`** clause appends payload columns strictly to the leaf pages without affecting the search tree structure.

data.title: Covering Index with INCLUDE Clause
data.content: Filters on username while returning email and created_at via Index-Only Scan.

data.text: An index-only scan is only possible when every column the query references is present in the index and the pages are marked all-visible in the visibility map. Run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` and look for the node `Index Only Scan`. The `Heap Fetches` counter tells you how often PostgreSQL still had to visit the table because the page was not all-visible.

data.title: Proving the heap is not touched
data.content: With a recently vacuumed table, heap fetches stay at zero and the plan reports an Index Only Scan.

data.title: Interview angle: index-only scans depend on VACUUM
data.text: A covering index does not guarantee an index-only scan. If the visibility map is stale — because autovacuum has not run since the last batch of updates — the planner must still check the heap, so the win disappears. That is the connection an interviewer is looking for between MVCC, VACUUM, and query performance: the same visibility map that makes an index-only scan possible is maintained by VACUUM.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Index-Only Scans eliminate table heap lookups.
Use `INCLUDE (col1, col2)` to attach non-search payload columns to leaf pages.
A clean Visibility Map (maintained via `VACUUM`) is required for Index-Only Scans.
